# Translate and Explain a Confusing Email or Letter with Perplexity

> **In short:** Open Perplexity, paste the confusing message, and ask it to translate, summarize, and draft a reply. Free to use on the web; Pro adds longer messages and file uploads. It can draft a reply, but it cannot send the email for you.

That long email from your landlord, the tax letter in German, the polite-but-passive-aggressive message from a client — they all sit in your inbox looking scary. Perplexity can turn any of them into two things you actually need: a plain-English summary of what they want, and a calm suggested reply you can edit before sending.

## Before you start
- A free Perplexity account (sign up with email, Google, or Apple) — works in any modern browser on phone or computer.
- The confusing message itself: either copied as text, or as a clear photo/screenshot (uploading may require Pro).
- About **5–8 minutes** for your first message, faster once you get the hang of it.
- Honest note: Perplexity is great at language and summarizing, but it's not a lawyer, accountant, or doctor. For official notices (taxes, contracts, legal threats), treat its summary as a starting point and confirm with a professional before you act.

## Step 1 — Open Perplexity and start a new thread
Go to **perplexity.ai** in your browser (or open the Perplexity app if you have it installed). On the home page you'll see a big text box in the middle that says something like **"Ask anything…"** — that's where the conversation happens. Click or tap inside the box once. A blinking cursor appears, and the page is ready for your question. If you're already signed in, you'll also see a small **"New Thread"** or **+** button at the top-left or top-right — tap it so your message doesn't mix with an older chat. If the layout looks different (Perplexity updates its design often), look for a clearly empty text area with a **Send** button (paper-plane icon ✈️ or arrow) at the end.
💬 Example: don't type yet — just leave the cursor blinking in the box.
You'll know it worked when the text box is empty, your cursor is blinking inside it, and no earlier conversation is showing above.

## Step 2 — Paste the confusing message into the chat
Open your email or letter in another tab, window, or app. Select **all the text** (Ctrl+A on Windows, Cmd+A on Mac, or long-press → Select All on a phone). Copy it (Ctrl+C / Cmd+C / Copy in the menu). Then tap back into Perplexity's text box and **paste** (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V / Paste). The full message lands inside the box as one block of text — you should see the words from the letter sitting there. If the message is very long, Perplexity may show a small character count or a warning; trim the greeting and signature if needed. If your screen looks different, you may also see a **paperclip icon 📎** or an **upload button** — that's for attaching files or photos of letters instead of pasting text.
💬 Example: paste a paragraph like "Sehr geehrte Mieter, wir möchten Sie daran erinnern, dass die Miete für November bis spätestens zum dritten Werktag des Monats zu überweisen ist…" — the exact wording matters, so paste the real thing.
You'll know it worked when the entire message shows up in the box, no strange symbols, and you can still see the send button (✈️ or arrow) at the end.

## Step 3 — Add a clear instruction below the pasted text
Don't hit send yet. Press **Enter** to make a new line inside the same box, then type what you want Perplexity to do with the message. Be specific — a vague "what does this mean?" gets a vague answer. The clearer the instruction, the more useful the reply. If you only see a single-line text box (some mobile views hide multi-line), look for a small **expand** icon or a **+** that opens a fuller composer. On the free plan you can usually ask anything; Pro users get longer pasted messages and file uploads — check the current plan details on Perplexity's pricing page if you're unsure which you have.
💬 Example: "Please translate this email into plain English, list the three things the sender wants me to do, and tell me how urgent it sounds."
You'll know it worked when the box contains both the pasted message **and** your instruction underneath, and you can read both clearly before sending.

## Step 4 — Send and read the summary
Tap the **Send** button (✈️ paper-plane icon, or an arrow ↵ at the end of the box). A short "thinking" animation appears — Perplexity is reading your message and writing its answer. After a few seconds, a reply appears under your message, with the translation at the top, then the bullet list of what the sender wants, then the urgency note. Skim it slowly: any word you don't understand, highlight and copy, then ask a follow-up like "What does [word] mean in everyday language?" If the answer doesn't quite hit the mark, click the small **Regenerate** button (often a circular arrow ↻ near the reply) to get a fresh attempt — sometimes the second version is clearer. If the screen looks different on your device, look for a **Rewrite**, **Try again**, or **New answer** button near the bottom of the reply.
💬 Example follow-up: "Can you explain 'bis spätestens zum dritten Werktag' like I'm 10 years old?"
You'll know it worked when you see a clear English version of the email, a short list of what the sender wants, and a plain-language sense of how urgent it really is.

## Step 5 — Ask for a suggested reply in the same chat
Stay in the **same conversation** (don't start a new thread) so Perplexity remembers the original message and its summary. In the text box at the bottom, type a request for a draft reply. Be polite about tone — Perplexity matches the energy you ask for. The reply will appear below your message, ready for you to copy. If you want a different vibe (firmer, more apologetic, more formal), just ask in a follow-up — it's faster than starting over. Free users can do this as many times as they want; Pro only matters if you need to paste very long messages or upload PDFs.
💬 Example: "Now write a short, polite reply in English confirming I'll pay by Friday and asking for a receipt."
You'll know it worked when a reply draft appears that you could realistically send after light editing — and you can copy it with a single tap or click.

## Step 6 — Copy, edit, and send the reply yourself
Highlight Perplexity's suggested reply and **copy** it (Ctrl+C / Cmd+C / long-press → Copy). Open your email app, start a new message, **paste** the draft into the body, and then **edit it in your own voice** — add your name, your real deadline, any details only you know. Perplexity can draft, but it cannot send email or access your inbox, so this last step is always yours. Read the whole thing once out loud before clicking send; if any sentence sounds weird in your voice, change it. If your interface looks different, look for a **Copy** icon (two overlapping squares 📋) at the corner of the reply, or simply long-press the reply on a phone to bring up the copy menu.
💬 Example edit: change "I will remit payment by Friday" to "I'll send the payment by Friday — thanks for the reminder, Maria."
You'll know it worked when you've sent a clear, calm reply that you actually wrote (with Perplexity's help), and the original confusing email no longer feels scary.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting without an instruction.** If you only paste the email and hit send, Perplexity may summarize it but won't translate or draft a reply. Always add a short instruction line under the paste — it changes the result completely.
- **Trusting the summary on legal or medical letters.** Perplexity can miss legal nuance. For tax notices, court letters, or anything health-related, treat its plain-English version as a heads-up, not a final answer — confirm with the right professional before paying or signing anything.
- **Sending the draft without editing.** AI-written text sometimes has odd phrasing, wrong names, or invented details. Always read the whole reply once, fix anything that doesn't sound like you, and remove anything that isn't true.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a long email from your bank, landlord, school, or insurance company lands in your inbox, you'll have a two-minute way to understand it and reply without stress — even if it arrives in another language.
- **For your business or work:** if clients or colleagues send you formal letters, contract updates, or foreign-language requests, you can draft a professional reply in the right tone in seconds, freeing you to focus on the actual decision rather than the wording.
- **If you're just getting started:** the easiest first move is to pick one email you've been ignoring because it felt too long or too formal, paste it into Perplexity, and ask for a three-bullet summary in plain English — that's it.

## Try it now
Open perplexity.ai, find one email you've been avoiding, paste it into the box, and type underneath: *"Translate this into plain English and give me three bullet points of what the sender actually wants from me."* Send it, read the result, and notice how much lighter the email feels five minutes later.
